en: open (to traffic or service); be connected

examples.ko: 새 지하철 노선이 다음 달에 개통돼요.
examples.en: The new subway line opens next month.
Travel became easier because the highway opened.
Once my phone is activated, I will text you right away.

examples.ko: 다리가 개통된 날 많은 사람이 구경하러 왔어요.
examples.en: Many people came to look on the day the bridge opened.
The internet has not been connected yet.

examples.ko: 공항까지 가는 철도가 곧 개통될 거예요.
examples.en: The railway to the airport will open soon.

explain: 길, 지하철, 전화, 인터넷 같은 것을 처음으로 쓸 수 있게 될 때 써요. 새 휴대폰을 사고 번호를 쓸 수 있게 하는 것도 '개통하다'라고 해요. '열리다'는 문이나 행사에, '개통되다'는 길과 통신에 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a road, subway, phone line or internet becomes usable for the first time. Activating a new phone number is also '개통하다'. '열리다' is for doors and events, while '개통되다' is for roads and communication lines.

dis.h: a road or line opens for use

p.n: 개통하다 needs someone who opens it as the subject.

examples.ko: 새로 만든 지하철 노선을 다음 달에 개통해요.
examples.en: They open the newly built subway line next month.
I bought a phone yesterday and activated it right away.

examples.ko: 고속도로가 개통하면 시간이 많이 줄 거예요.
examples.en: When the highway opens, it will save a lot of time.
I called to get the internet set up at home.
The mayor came on the day the bridge opened.
When will this road open?

explain: 길, 다리, 지하철 노선이 처음 열려 다닐 수 있게 될 때 써요. 휴대폰과 인터넷은 신청한 뒤 쓸 수 있게 되는 것을 '개통'이라고 해요. 휴대폰 가게에서는 '열다' 대신 '개통'이라고 말하고, 막혔던 길이 다시 열리면 '재개통'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when a road, bridge or subway line opens to traffic for the first time. For phones and internet, 개통 means the service is switched on after you sign up. In a phone shop people say 개통, not 열다, and a road that reopens is 재개통.

dis.h: open a road or line for use

p.n: The passive cannot take an object marked with 를.

examples.ko: 졸업 여행을 가려고 버스를 한 대 대절했어요.
examples.en: We chartered a bus for our graduation trip.

examples.ko: 회사에서 행사 때 관광버스를 대절하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to charter a tour bus for the event.

examples.ko: 가족 모임이라 작은 버스를 대절하면 편해요.
examples.en: It's a family gathering, so chartering a small bus is convenient.

examples.ko: 택시를 대절해서 하루 종일 섬을 구경했어요.
examples.en: We hired a taxi for the whole day and toured the island.

examples.ko: 버스를 대절할 때는 미리 가격을 물어봐야 해요.
examples.en: When you charter a bus, you should ask about the price in advance.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 사람들은 버스를 대절해 단체로 응원을 갔어요.
examples.en: The people in our neighborhood chartered a bus and went to cheer as a group.

explain: 버스, 택시, 배처럼 탈것을 통째로 빌릴 때 써요. 자리 하나만 사서 타는 것과는 달라서 앞에는 보통 '버스를', '택시를'이 와요. '전세 내다'라고도 말하지만, 집을 빌리는 '전세'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: Use it when you rent a whole vehicle such as a bus, taxi or boat, not just one seat. The object before it is usually '버스를' or '택시를'. People also say '전세 내다', but don't confuse that with '전세', the housing lease.

en: go around; go round; tour; make the rounds

examples.en: The teacher goes around the classroom helping students.
The nurse makes the rounds of the wards one by one.
The doctor went around the islands seeing patients.
This bus is a route that circles the tourist spots.
Our team plans to tour the whole country.
Who was the person who went around the village yesterday?

explain: 정해진 곳을 차례로 돌 때 써요. '돌아다니다'는 자유롭게 다니는 느낌이라 달라요. '순찰하다'는 경찰이나 경비가 안전을 살피러 돌 때 주로 쓰고, '순회하다'는 가르치거나 공연하거나 진료하러 돌 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used for going around set places in order. 돌아다니다 feels free and aimless, so it differs. 순찰하다 is mostly for police or guards checking safety, while 순회하다 also covers going around to teach, perform, or treat patients.

examples.en: This is the planned site where a new park will be built.
Residents near the planned factory site are opposing it.
Land prices went up in the area announced as the planned site.
I went and saw the planned new-town site in person.

examples.ko: 공사 예정지 앞에 안내판이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A notice board stands in front of the planned construction site.

examples.ko: 새 집 이사 예정지가 회사에서 너무 멀어요.
examples.en: The place we plan to move to is too far from my office.

explain: '건설 예정지, 개발 예정지, 이주 예정지'처럼 앞말과 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요. '후보지'는 아직 고르는 중인 곳이고, '예정지'는 그곳으로 하기로 이미 정해진 곳을 말해요.
explain_en: It is usually combined with a preceding word, as in '건설 예정지', '개발 예정지' or '이주 예정지'. A '후보지' is a candidate still being chosen, while an '예정지' is a place already decided on.

examples.en: The new library will be completed next month.
The apartment building was completed later than planned.

examples.ko: 다리가 완공되면 출퇴근이 훨씬 편해질 거예요.
examples.en: Once the bridge is completed, commuting will be much easier.

examples.ko: 완공된 건물에는 아직 사람이 살지 않아요.
examples.en: Nobody lives in the completed building yet.

examples.ko: 긴 공사 끝에 드디어 공장이 완공되었어요.
examples.en: After a long construction period, the factory was finally completed.
When is the school gym scheduled to be completed?

explain: 완공되다는 건물·다리·도로처럼 지어지는 것이 주어일 때 써요. 짓는 회사나 사람이 주어이면 '완공하다'를 써요. 그림·요리·숙제 같은 작은 것에는 '완공' 대신 '완성되다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 완공되다 takes the thing being built (a building, bridge, road) as its subject. If the builder is the subject, use 완공하다. For small things like a painting, a dish or homework, 완성되다 sounds more natural than 완공.

p.n: 준공 is the official or legal term, as in a completion inspection.

en: fly or sail on a route; operate (flights, ships)

examples.en: This ship runs to Jeju Island every day.

examples.ko: 비행기가 안개 때문에 운항할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The plane could not fly because of the fog.
Passenger ferries do not operate when a typhoon comes.

examples.ko: 이 항공사는 새벽에도 운항하는 노선이 있어요.
examples.en: This airline has routes that operate even at dawn.
The captain sailed ships for thirty years.

examples.ko: 지금은 하루에 세 번 운항하고 있어요.
examples.en: It currently makes three runs a day.

explain: 비행기와 배가 정해진 길로 다닌다는 뜻이에요. 버스와 지하철은 '운행하다'라고 해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 하늘과 바다는 '운항', 땅 위는 '운행'이에요.
explain_en: It means planes and ships travel along a set route. Buses and subways use '운행하다', which is easy to mix up: '운항' is for sky and sea, '운행' is for land.

dis.h: planes or ships run on a route

p.n: 운항하다 stresses regular service on a route. 날다 just describes flying.

examples.en: This bus runs from 5 a.m.

examples.ko: 눈이 와서 지하철이 천천히 운행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of the snow, the subway is running slowly.
Some routes don't run on public holidays.
Is there a bus that runs at night too?

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 기차가 모두 운행되지 않았어요.
examples.en: No trains ran because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 이 열차는 하루에 열 번 운행될 거예요.
examples.en: This train will run ten times a day.

explain: 버스, 지하철, 기차, 배처럼 정해진 길을 다니는 탈것에 써요. 개인 차를 몰면 '운전하다'라고 하고, '운행'은 운영하는 쪽 입장이에요. 짝말은 '운행이 중단되다'예요.
explain_en: For buses, subways, trains and ships that follow set routes. Driving your own car is '운전하다'; '운행' is from the operator's side. A common pairing is '운행이 중단되다'.

dis.h: passive: buses or trains are in service

p.n: Almost the same; 운행하다 is the active form.

examples.en: A mobile library comes to our neighborhood every week.

examples.ko: 이동도서관 덕분에 섬 아이들도 책을 빌려 봐요.
examples.en: Thanks to the mobile library, island kids can borrow books too.
I looked around a mobile library made from a converted bus.
I borrowed two storybooks from the mobile library.
When does the mobile library come to our village?

examples.ko: 이동도서관 직원이 어린이 책을 추천해 줬어요.
examples.en: A mobile library worker recommended a children's book to me.

explain: 책을 차에 싣고 다니면서 사람들이 사는 곳을 찾아가는 도서관이에요. 일반 도서관과 달리 한곳에 고정되어 있지 않아서 오는 요일과 장소를 미리 확인해야 해요. 보통 '이동도서관이 오다', '이동도서관에서 빌리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a library that carries books in a vehicle and goes to where people live. Unlike a regular library it isn't fixed in one place, so you need to check its day and location in advance. Typical patterns are '이동도서관이 오다' and '이동도서관에서 빌리다'.

examples.ko: 이 공항에서는 밤에 비행기가 이착륙하지 않아요.
examples.en: Planes don't take off or land at this airport at night.
The drone took off and landed safely on the rooftop.
My ears feel blocked when the plane takes off and lands.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 오면 헬기가 이착륙하기 어려워요.
examples.en: When it snows a lot, it's hard for helicopters to take off and land.
Even small planes take off and land on this runway.

examples.ko: 하루에 수백 대가 이착륙하는 큰 공항이에요.
examples.en: It's a big airport where hundreds of planes take off and land every day.

explain: '이륙하다'와 '착륙하다'를 함께 말하는 동사예요. '비행기가 이착륙하다'처럼 목적어 없이 써요. 한 동작만 말할 때는 '이륙하다'나 '착륙하다'를 쓰세요.
explain_en: This verb covers both '이륙하다' (take off) and '착륙하다' (land). It is used without an object, as in '비행기가 이착륙하다'. If you mean only one action, use '이륙하다' or '착륙하다'.

examples.en: I ate lunch at the school cafeteria.

examples.ko: 카페테리아에서는 먼저 쟁반을 들고 줄을 서요.
examples.en: At a cafeteria, you first pick up a tray and line up.
The company cafeteria menu is decent today.
I had coffee with a friend at the cafeteria.
There is a cafeteria in the basement of this building.
The cafeteria was crowded, so I couldn't find a seat.

explain: '카페'와 달리 음식을 직접 골라 담아 먹는 식당이에요. 학교는 '학생식당', 회사는 '구내식당'이라고도 말해요. 외국 영화나 학교 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Unlike a '카페', it is a place where you pick and carry your own food. At schools people also say '학생식당', and at companies '구내식당'. You often hear it in stories about foreign schools.
